description: §14.8.9 — `Response.redirect(...)` in a `protect=` file COMPILES (it carries no body, so there is nothing the egress floor could fail to inspect) but fires W-PROTECT-005 (warning), because the RUNTIME guard still refuses it: Bun gives redirect/error a 0-byte ReadableStream rather than a null body, and a secret-carrying `new Response(body, {status:302, headers:{Location}})` is indistinguishable from one at the exit. The seam is reported at build time instead of surfacing as a 500 on the first request.
rationale: E-PROTECT-005's rationale is that a hand-serialized BODY is an opaque stream the floor cannot read; a null-body construction has no such stream, so firing the hard error on `Response.redirect` / `Response.error` contradicts the diagnostic's own justification — and because that gate has no escape hatch, it made redirects impossible in any `protect=` app, including one whose SELECT projects every protected column out (this case does exactly that: `SELECT id, name`, no protected column). But permitting them SILENTLY would swap a loud build error for a runtime 500, which is a worse defect, so the compile-time warning names the gap and gives the exact rewrite (`new Response(not, { status: 302, headers: { Location: ... } })`) that the runtime guard recognizes via `.body === null`. Paired with `null-body-response-clean`, which shows that rewrite compiling warning-free.
